description: Conformance corpus for accessor members: namespace members whose value the host computes on every read, and optionally stores on every write. Every runtime builds the `clock` probe host below, runs each case's script in a fresh runtime with a fresh probe, and asserts the outcome.
notes: `clock.now` is a getter that counts its own calls and returns the new count, so the first read in a runtime is 1. Constructing the runtime and freezing the namespace must not call it.
`clock.speed` is a getter/setter pair over one stored value that starts at 1. The setter records every value it receives, in order.
`clock.broken`'s getter throws an error whose message is `clock offline`. `clock.jammed`'s getter returns 0 and its setter throws an error whose message is `rejected value`.
`phase` is a top-level accessor whose getter returns `day`. A top-level accessor is a global accessor property that cannot be deleted or redefined.
`clock.locked` is provided but gated by `clock.admin`, which is not granted. `clock.absent` is optional and not provided. `clock.gone` is not optional and not provided.
Assigning to an accessor declared `get` throws a `TypeError` whose message contains `read-only`, in strict and sloppy code alike, and does not call the getter.

A getter or setter call is a binding call: it is capability-gated on every access, it runs on the calling script's execution budget, and an error the host throws reaches the script as that runtime's ordinary binding error, catchable, with the host's message in it.

`expect.result` is compared as JSON. `expect.error` lists substrings the surfaced error message must contain. `expect.limit` means `execute` must fail with the runtime's execution-limit error. `expect.reads` is how many times the `clock.now` getter ran. `expect.writes` is the list of values the `clock.speed` setter received.

speed.description: The tick speed, read and written live.

cases.name: the getter runs on every read
a read is never cached
cases.script: var a = clock.now; var b = clock.now; b - a

cases.name: the setter receives the assigned value
assignment without a setter throws in sloppy code
cases.script: var out; try { clock.now = 9; out = 'assigned'; } catch (e) { out = [e instanceof TypeError, e.message.indexOf('read-only') >= 0]; } out

cases.name: assignment without a setter throws in strict code
cases.script: (function () { 'use strict'; try { clock.now = 9; return 'assigned'; } catch (e) { return [e instanceof TypeError, e.message.indexOf('read-only') >= 0]; } })()

cases.name: a refused assignment leaves the value live
a getter error reaches the script as a binding error
cases.script: var out; try { clock.broken; out = 'read'; } catch (e) { out = e.message.indexOf('clock offline') >= 0; } out

cases.name: an uncaught getter error fails the script
a setter error reaches the script as a binding error
cases.script: var out; try { clock.jammed = 3; out = 'written'; } catch (e) { out = e.message.indexOf('rejected value') >= 0; } out

cases.name: a gated accessor refuses the read
cases.script: var out; try { clock.locked; out = 'read'; } catch (e) { out = e.message.indexOf('clock.admin') >= 0; } out

cases.name: an omitted optional accessor is undefined
an omitted non-optional accessor throws on read
an accessor is a real accessor property on a frozen namespace
cases.script: var d = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(clock, 'now'); [Object.isFrozen(clock), typeof d.get, 'value' in d, d.enumerable, Object.keys(clock).indexOf('now') >= 0]

cases.name: a top-level accessor reads live and refuses assignment
cases.script: var refused; try { phase = 'night'; refused = false; } catch (e) { refused = e instanceof TypeError; } var d = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(globalThis, 'phase'); [phase, refused, typeof d.get, d.configurable]

cases.name: a getter loop is stopped by the execution budget
